Endangered Animals

Today, there are some endangered animals on Earth. It means that we can find only a few of
them around us. Some examples are whales, pandas, tigers and Asian elephants.

Humans destroy the natural homes of the animals in the forests, lakes and plains. When the

destroy lakes. They make homes and roads instead. Then the animals wont have a place to live.

Simple ways to protect wildlife
شیوه هاب ساده برای محافظت از حیات وحش
One easy way to protect wildlife is learning about the endangered animals that live around
you. Teach your friends and family about the wonderful birds, fish and plants that live near your
home. In this way, they are going to be more careful about nature. You can also visit a national
wildlife museum or park. These places give good information about how to protect endangered
animals and their homes. You can do voluntary work in these places to help animals and their
babies.

Another thing you can do is protecting the natural home of the endangered animals. When you
keep nature clean and safe, the animals will live longer. Protecting the trees of forests is also
helpful. If you live in a village, you need to be very careful about the hunters who come to your
village to hurt animals. Whenever you see these people, you need to call the police. These are
simple things, but they will help nature a lot.

Dolphins are among the smaller whales. Most live in salt water oceans, but some live in rivers.
There are oceanic dolphins and river dolphins. Dolphins are from 1.5 meters to 4 meters long, but
the largest dolphin, the killer whale, can be up to 8 meters long. It is now known to be a mammal
and quite an intelligent mammal. Dolphins breathe air. A dolphins nose is on top of his head so
the dolphin can easily breathe on the surface of the water.
The skin of a dolphin has no scales. It is soft and smooth. They are very social and help each
other fight off sea hunters. They have fought off sharks in this way. They look after the young
when the mothers need to leave them to hunt for food. The young need to breathe more often than
the adults, and the food may be in deeper waters.

A Wonderful Liquid
یک مایع شگفت ر ن
انگی
The human body is a real wonder. It is sometimes good to think about our body and how it
works. Our body is doing millions of jobs all the time.
انگی است .ن
بعیص مواقع خوبه که درمورد بدنمان و اینکه چگونه کار می کند ،فکر کنیم .بدن ما داره میلیونها بدن انسان ها واقعأ شگفت ر ن
کار رو به طور هم زمان انجام میده.
One of the most important parts of the body is blood. The heart pumps this red liquid around
the body. This keeps us healthy and alive.
یگ از مهمیین بخش های بدنمان خون است .قلب این مایع قرمز رنگ را در رستارس بدن پمپاژ یمکند .این کار ما را سالم و زنده نگه
می دارد.
More than half of blood is plasma. This is a clear and yellow liquid. It carries red and white
cells. There are millions of red blood cells in one small drop of blood. They carry oxygen round
the body and collect carbon dioxide from body parts. There are thousands of white cells in a drop
of blood. They are bigger than red cells. They defend our body against microbes.

بدن جمع آوری یمکنند .هزاران سلول سفید در یک قطره از خون وجود دارد .آنها بزرگی از سلول های قرمز هستند که از بدن در برابر

This wonderful liquid is a great gift from Allah. We can thank Allah by keeping our body
healthy. One way to do that is eating healthy food and doing daily exercises. Another way is to
donate our blood to those who need it.

Microbes
میکروب ها
Microbes are really wonderful. They are everywhere! They live all around you, on you and
inside you! Microbes are very small, so you cant see them. But dont worry. Some microbes
make you sick but most others keep you healthy and even help you to fight disease.

می کنند .میکروب ها خیلی کوچک هستند بنابراین شما نم توانید آنها را ببینید .اما نگران نباشید .تعدادی از میکروب ها شما را مریض می

There are so many different types of microbes. We still dont really know how many there are
but we know that microbes do lots of different things. Bacteria and viruses are two important
types of microbes.

Bacteria are really important microbes. They are very small. They have only one cell. Bacteria
can live in any area of the earth. They arent all bad; in fact, you couldnt live without some
!bacteria

همک آنها بد نیستند .در حقیقت ،شما نم توانستید بدون تعدادی از ر ی روی کره ز
باکیی ها زندگ کنید. زمت زندگ کنند.
Viruses are among the smallest microbes on the earth, even smaller than bacteria. They are
different from bacteria because they cannot live on their own. Viruses need to be inside a living
cell to live and grow. There arent many good things about viruses - they usually attack your body

Iran is a four- season country and tourists can find a range of activities from skiing to desert
touring in different parts of the country. Many Muslims also travel to Iran and go to holy shrines
in Mashhad, Qom and Shiraz. Iranian people are hospitable and kind to travelers and tourists .

بایست به نسبت تعداد ابزار شنیداری (گوش) به ابزار گفتاری (دهان ) ،به اجرای تمرینهای مرتبط بپردازیم .به عبارت دیگر ،ما به
عنوان زبان آموز موظفیم که دو برابر زمانی را که به تمرین مهارت سخن گفتن speakingمی پردازیم ،به تمرین مهارت شنیدن
یا listeningاختصاص دهیم.
پیش از معرفی شیوه های تقویت مهارت شنیداری ،لازم است به برخی از موانع و مشکلات زبان آموزان در ارتباط با مهارت
شنیداری اشاره ای کنیم

در حقیقت ،دشواری ظاهری زبان و همچنین عدم توجه کافی و لازم نظام های آموزشی به این مهارت بسیار مهم موجب می
شود که بسیاری از زبان آموزان یادگیری listeningآن طور که باید و شاید توانمند نشوند و متعاقداً دیگر مهارت های ایشان ،از
جمله سخن گفتن ( ، )speakingنیز تحث تأثیر قرار گیرد .در واقع ،آنچه تسلط بر listeningرا به تجربه ای لذت بخش برای
زبان آموزان تبدیل می کند ،این است که ما به عنوان زبان آموزان زبان دوم ،سوم و ....نمی بایست به دنبال درک کلیه جزئیات یک
متن شنیداری باشیم .آنچه در وهله اول مهم به نظر می رسد ،درک کلیات و رئوس مطالب است.
تجربه نشان داده است زبان آموزانی که در مراحل اولیه تمرین های شنیداری خود به کلیات توجه بیشتری می کنند ،در مقایسه
با کسانی که به دنبال جزئیات هستند ،توانایی بیشتری در درک جزئیات در تمرینهای بعدی خود دارند.
در صورتی که زبان آموزان در حین گوش فرا دادن به تمرین ها ی listeningمکلامات را به زبان مادری خود ترجمه کند ،مانعی
بر سر راه شنیدن و درک او ایجاد می شود .این کار به منزله مانعی میان متکلم (خواه فرد و خواه رادیو تلویزیون و شنونده است
زیرا زمانی که فرد شنونده به ترجمه مکلامات می پردازد ،از توجه به مابقی مکلامه غافل خواهد شد و در نتیجه ،فرایند ارتباطی به

قانون کلی مهارت شنیداری a+1است .این قانون می گوید که باید همواره از یک سطح بالاتر از خودمان شروع کنیم .این بدان
معناست که اگر زبان آموزی در سطح مقدماتی beginnerاست ،باید به مطالبی گوش کند که در سطح پیش متوسط باشد و اگر
در سطح متوسط است ،به مطالبی که در سطح متوسط رو به بالا است گوش فرا دهد تا مهارت شنیداریاش تقویت شود.

اما این سؤال پیش می آید که کدام مواد آموزشی می توانند برای ما مؤثر باشند یا به عدارت دیگر ،ما چگونه باید سطح خود را
تعیین کنیم .کاری که برای مشخص سازی سطح خود می توانیم انجام دهیم این است که پیش از تهیه کتاب یا متن ،تعداد 1۰۰
واژه از یک بند را انتخاب کنیم.
نمی بایست کلیه واژگان ،اعم از and, butغیره را مد نظر قرار دهیم .حال اگر از این صد واژه انتخابی معنی پنج تا ده واژه را
ندانیم ،متن مورد نظر مناسب ماست ،در صورتی که این تعداد بیشتر باشد ،متن دشوارتر از سطح ماست و چنانچه با هیچ واژه جدید
روبه رو نشویم ،متن برای ما آسان است .در واقع ،اگر سطح زبان ما 4۰باشد ،سطح کتاب انتخابی می بایست 10 + 40باشد.
به زبان آموزان توصیه می شود که اگر در سطح متوسط یا متوسط رو به پایین هستند ،به هیچ وجه از متون اخبار انگلیسی
استفاده نکنند؛ چرا که با این کار تنها به گویش رسمی و استاندارد زبان مقصد عادت می کنند و از دید آموزشی ،گوششان به اصطالح
تنبل می شود .گوش دادن به اخبار به زبان آموزان سطوح بالا توصیه می شود.
نحوه تقویت حافظه کوتاه مدت
آیا تا به حال از خود پرسیده اید که بزرگترین مشکل شما در مهارت شنیداری چیست؟
تجربه نشان می دهد که در موارد زیادی زبان آموزان حافظه کوتاه مدت ضعیفی دارند؛ درواقع ،هنگامی که سعی می کنند جمله
ای را که شنیده اند ضبط و تجزیه و تحلیل کنند ،جمله ای دیگر اضافه می شود و همین سبب می گردد که آنان نتوانند مفهوم را
درک کنند .ما برای تقویت حافظه کوتاه مدت خود می توانیم از تمرین های زیر استفاده کنیم
در تمرین اول ،زبان آموزان می بایست ۵۰واژه را به طور تصادفی انتخاب کرده و آنها را با صدای خود ضبط کند .سپس یک
بار به فایل صوتی گوش دهد و هر آنچه را به خاطر می آورد ،یادداشت کند.
در تمرین دوم ،زبان آموزان می بایست فایلی را متناسب با سطح زبانی خود انتخاب کند و به آن گوش دهند .سپس در هر ده
ثانیه یک بار فایل صوتی را متوقف کنند و هر آنچه را به خاطر می آورند ،بازگو کنند.
در تمرین سوم که باید به صورت گروهی انجام شود ،زبان آموزان بایستی موضوعی را که مورد عالقه ایشان است ،انتخاب و
شروع به صحبت در مورد آن کنند .سپس سعی کنند به خاطر آورند که اولین سؤال چه بوده ،آخرین واژه سؤال دوم چه بوده ،سؤال
سوم با چه کلمه ای شروع شده است و ...در حقیقت این کار موجب می شود که زبان آموزان در حین صحبت کردن نسبت به
جملات و کلمات هوشیار باشند.
نحوه استفاده از فایل های صوب
همواره تمرین های ابتدایی برای تقویت مهارت شنیداری باید همراه با استفاده از فایلهای صوتی همراه با متن باشد.
گام اول :یک بار با دقت متن را می خوانیم و واژگانی را که معنی آنها را نمی دانیم ،پیدا می کنیم.
گام دوم :ده ثانیه به فایل صوتی گوش می دهیم و هر آنچه را به خاطر می آوریم ،بازگو می کنیم.
گام سوم :ده ثانیه به فایل صوتی گوش می دهیم و سعی می کنیم متن را پیاده یا transcribeکنیم .چنانچه بخشی را متوجه
نشدیم ،جای آن را خالی می گذاریم .سپس به ده ثانیه بعدی گوش می دهیم.
گام چهارم :دوباره به فایل صوتی گوش می دهیم ،متن خود را با متن اصلی تطبیق می دهیم و هر آنچه را در مرحله پیش متوجه
نشده ایم،از روی متن اصلی پر می کنیم.
راهکارهای جانت
در حقیقت ،زبان آموزانی که برای مثال می توانند در حین غذا خورد هم زمان به یک فایل صوتی یا اخبار هم گوش دهند ،از
مهارت شنیداری خوبی برخوردارند.
یکی از راه های مؤثر برای تقویت مهارت شنیداری این است که زبان آموزان برای مثال زبان انگلیسی ،محیط پیرامون خود را با
موسیقی ،اخبار ،داستان و ...به زبان انگلیسی پر کنند .پیشنهاد می شوند پس از یک ماه تمرین مهارت شنیداری ،به منظور افزایش
حساسیت شنیداری صدای دستگاه خود را تا حد ممکن کم کنید
این کار موجب می شودکه با حساسیت بیشتری به اصوات گوش دهید.

sections.title: تمرین دیگری که پس از یک ماه تمرین شنیداری می توانیم انجام دهیم این است که پس از گوش دادن به فایل صوتی ،لحن
lines: گوینده را تقلید کرده و در مراحل بعدی سعی کنیم جمله ای را که شنیده ایم با تغییر صدا و لحن خود به گونه های متفاوتی بازگو
کنیم .فایده این کار آن است که زبان آموز با لحن های مختلف آشنا می شود .در واقع ،او آنچه را می شنود ،با دانش زبانی خود
تطبیق می دهد و چنانچه تشابهی پیدا نکند ،این حس برایش پیش می آید که فایل صوتی از واژگان جدید تشکیل شده است .این
در حالی است که زبان آموز واژه را می داند اما گوینده آن را به نحوی ادا می کند که برای زبان آموز جدید است .از همین رو تمرین
بیشتر احتمال بروز چنین مشکلاتی را به حداقل می رساند.
پس از آنکه زبان آموز در مهارت شنیداری به سطح قابل قبولی رسید ،پیشنهاد می شود که به جای فیلم یا فایل صوتی و متن
بیشتر به منابع صوتی همچون رادیو یا کتاب های صوتی گوش دهد ،چرا که هنگام دیدن فیلم برای درک مطلب از تصاویر هم کمک
می گیرد.

اجزاء کلام در زبان انگلییس یا همان نقش کلمه در جمله ،به ۸قسمت متمایز میشوند که از لحاظ کاربرد و معنا نقش
خاصی را در جملههای زبان انگلیسی ایفا میکنند .ما از هزاران کلمه در صحبتهای روزمره خود استفاده میکنیم و خوب است که
بدانیم تمام این کلمات را میتوانیم در ۸دسته گروهبندی کنیم .یادگیری عناصر زبان و نقش آنها ،در یادگیری ساختار جملههای از
اهمیت بالایی برخوردار است
)1اسم در زبان انگلییس(Noun)
اسم کلمه ای است که برای نامیدن اشخاص ،حیوانات ،اشیا ،اماکن و یا حالات آنها به کار می رود.
ضمی در زبان انگلییس(Pronoun)
ضمیر کلمه ای است که جانشین اسم میگردد ،و ما را از تکرار اسامی اشخاص و اشیا و غیره بینیاز میکند.
)3صفت در زبان انگلییس(Adjective)
صفت کلمه ای است که اسم را توصیه می کند و معنی آن را روشن تر و مشخص تر و کامل تر بیان میکند.
)4فعل در زبان انگلییس(Verb)
فعل کلمه ای است که عمل یا حالتی را بیان میکنند .
)5قید در زبان انگلییس(Adverb)
قید کلمه ای است که برای توصیف فعل ،صفت و یا قید دیگر به کار می رود ،در واقع قید حالت و چگونگی انجام یک فعل و
وضعیت یک صفت یا قید دیگر را بیان میکند.
)۶حرف اضافه در زبان انگلییس(Preposition)
حرف اضافه کلمه ای است که نسبت یا ارتباط اسم و ضمیر را با سایر قسمتهای جمله نشان میدهد .معموال از حروف اضافه
برای نشان دادن مکان ،زمان و جهت و … استفاده میشود .
)7حرف ربط در زبان انگلییس(Conjunction)
حرف ربط کلمه ای است که برای وصل کردن دو شبه جمله ،دو عبارت و یا دو کلمه به کار می رود.
)8صوت در زبان انگلییس(Interjection)
کلمه ای است که برای تعجب و تحسین افسوس و وحشت و سایر احساسات ناگهانی و تند مورد استفاده قرار میگیرد ،و انواع آن
!Hey!, wow!, hush!, ah!, oh عبارتند از
در این جزوه ،به طور کافی در مورد ضمایر ،حروف اضافه ،حروف ربط توضیح داده شده است .حروف صوت هم که در حیطه کنکور

sections.title: English to English Dictionary (Lesson One)
lines: 1. alive / əˈlaɪv / adj. living; not dead
• Are your grandparents alive?
2. among / əˈmʌŋ / prep. in the middle of a group of people or things
• I often feel nervous when Im among strangers.
3. animal / ˈænɪməl / n. any living thing that can move and feel but is not a bird, or an insect
• Cats, horses and rats are animals.
4. around / əˈraʊnd / adv. in or to different places or in different directions
• The children were running around the house.
5. based on / beɪsd ʌn / v. according to
• The film is based on a true story.
6. beautiful / ˈbjuːt əfəl / adj. very nice to see, hear or smell
• Flowers are beautiful.
7. boring / ˈbɔːrɪŋ / adj. not interesting; tiring
• That lesson was so boring!
8. building / ˈbɪld ɪŋ / n. a structure with a roof and walls. Houses, schools are all buildings.
• The enemy soldiers destroyed the buildings.
9. buy / baɪ / v. to give money to get something; purchase
• I will buy that new bicycle.
10. careful / ˈkeəfəl / adj. thinking about what you are doing so that you do not make a mistake or have
an accident
• Be careful! Theres a car coming.
11. chart / tʃɑːrt / n. a drawing that gives information about something
• The doctor recorded her blood pressure on a chart.
12. circle / ˈsɜːkəl / n. a round shape; a ring
• There are 360 degrees in a circle.
v. to draw a circle around something
• Circle the answer you think is correct.
13. common / ˈkɒmən / adj. happening often or found in many places
• Jackson is a common English name.
14. correct / kəˈrekt / adj. right or true; with no mistakes
• All your answers were correct.
v. to show or tell someone that something is wrong and to make it right
• Students said it was helpful if the teacher corrected their pronunciation.
15. country / ˈkʌntri / n. an area of land with its own people and government
• France and Spain are European countries.
16. cut / kʌt / v. to break or damage sth with something sharp, for example a knife or scissors
• I cut the apple in half.
17. danger / ˈdeɪndʒər / n. the possibility of harm or death to someone; risk
• Smoking is a danger to health.
18. daughter / ˈdɔː.tər / n. a girl or woman who is somebodys child
• Liz and Phil have a daughter and three sons
19. destroy / diˈstrɔɪ / v. to damage something so badly that it cannot be used
• A bomb fell on the building and destroyed it.
20. die / daɪ / v. to stop living; People, animals and plants die if they dont have water.
• She died of cancer.
21. different / ˈdɪfrənt / adj. not the same
• These two shoes are different sizes!
22. dry / draɪ / adj. with no water or liquid in it or on it
• These plants grow well in dry soil / a dry climate.
23. endangered / ɪnˈdeɪndʒərd / adj. animals or plants that may soon not exist
• endangered birds/plants/species
24. enough / ə ˈnʌf / adv. as much or as many as you need; sufficient
• There isnt enough food for ten people.
25. especially / ɪ ˈspeʃəli / adv. more than usual or more than others
• She loves animals, especially horses.
26. exam / eɡˈzæm / n. a test of what you know or can do; test
• Weve got an English exam next week.
27. example / eɡˈzæmp əl / n. sth that shows what other things of the same kind are like
• This dictionary gives many examples of how words are used in sentences.
28. forest / ˈfɒrɪst / n. a large area of land covered with trees
• We went for a walk in the forest.
29. future / ˈfjuː.tʃər / n. a period of time that is to come
• Sometimes I worry about the future.
30. gulf / ɡʌlf / n. a large part of the sea that has land almost all the way around it
• the Persian Gulf and the countries around it
31. happy / ˈhæpi / adj. feeling, showing, or causing pleasure or satisfaction; glad
• She looks very happy.
32. hard-working / hɑːrdˈwɜːkɪŋ / adj. always doing a lot of work
• She was always very hard-working at school.
33. hear / hɪər / v. to notice sounds with your ears
• My grandfather is getting old and cant hear very well.
34. helpful / ˈhelpfəl / adj. willing to help, or useful
• Im sorry, I was only trying to be helpful.
35. here / hɪər / adv. in, at or to this place
• London is only 50 miles from here.
36. hope / həʊp / v. to want something to happen or be true
• I hope that you will have a nice holiday.
37. hot / hɑːt / n. having a high temperature
• Im hot. Can you open the window?
38. hunt / hʌnt / v. to chase animals to kill them as a sport or for food
• Some animals hunt at night.
• Young lions have to learn to hunt.
39. hunter / ˈhʌn.tər / n. a person or an animal that hunts animals for food or for sport
• Animals in the cat family are hunters.
40. hurt / hɜːrt / n. to make somebody or something feel pain
• Hard work never hurt anyone.
41. increase / ɪnˈkriːs / v. to (make something) become larger in amount or size
• The number of women who go out to work has increased.
42. information / ɪnfəˈmeɪʃən / n. facts about a situation, person, event, etc.
• Do you have any information about/on train times?
• Modern computers can hold huge amounts of information.
43. injured / ˈɪndʒərd / adj. hurt or physically harmed
• The injured woman was taken to hospital.
44. instead / ɪn ˈsted / adv. in place of someone or something else
• Theres no coffee. Would you like a cup of tea instead?
45. kill / kɪl / v. to cause someone or something to die
• Food must be heated to a high temperature to kill harmful bacteria.
46. lake / leɪk / n. a big area of water with land all around it
• We used to go boating on that lake.
47. learn / lɜːrn / v. to get knowledge or skill in a new subject or activity
• When did you learn to swim?
48. lose / luːz / v. not to be able to find something
• Hes always losing his car keys.
49. mountain / ˈmaʊntɪn / n. a very high hill
• Everest is the highest mountain in the world.
50. museum / mjuːˈziːəm / n. a building where people can look at old or interesting things
• The museum is full of rare and precious treasures.
51. national / ˈnæʃənəl / adj. connected with all of a country; typical of a country
• Britain has more than ten national newspapers.
52. natural / ˈnætʃərəl / adj. made by nature, not by people
• Floods and earthquakes are natural disasters.
53. nature / ˈneɪtʃər / n. the way a person or thing is
• I came out here to enjoy nature.
54. near / nɪər / adj. not far away; close to somebody or something
• Lets walk to my house. Its quite near.
55. pain / peɪn / n. a feeling of physical suffering caused by injury or illness
• Her eyes were full of pain.
56. passage / ˈpæsɪdʒ / n. a short piece of writing that is part of a larger piece of work; text
• Kathy read a short passage from the Bible.
57. place / ˈpleɪs / n. a particular area or position; site
• Put the book back in the right place.
58. plural / ˈplʊərəl / n. the form of a word that shows there is more than one
• The plural of child is children.
59. poem / ˈpəʊɪm / n. words arranged in lines in an artistic way
• He wrote poems about the beauty of the countryside.
60. point / pɔɪnt / n. the purpose of, or the reason for, doing something
• The point of going to school is to learn.
61. program / ˈprəʊ ɡræm / n. a. a set of instructions that you give to a computer
• Load the program into the computer.
62. proper / ˈprɒpər / adj. right or correct, suitable
• She likes everything to be in its proper place.
63. protect / prəˈtekt / v. to keep somebody or something safe
• Parents try to protect their children from danger.
64. put out / pʊt aʊt / v. to stop a fire or a light burning; extinguish
• It took the firefighters several hours to put out the flames.
65. rain / reɪn / n. drops of water from clouds
• The water level in the lake is much higher after heavy rain.
v. If it rains, water falls from the sky in small drops
• Its raining hard/heavily.
66. really / ˈrɪəli / adv. in fact; actually
• He isnt really angry - hes just pretending.
67. recently / ˈriːsəntli / adv. not long ago; lately
• Have you seen any good films recently?
68. relative / ˈrelətɪv / n. a member of your family
• All her close/distant relatives came to the wedding.
69. road / rəʊd / n. the way from one place to another, where cars can go
• Is this the road to the city centre?
70. safe / seɪf / adj. not in danger; not hurt
• Dont go out alone at night – you wont be safe.
71. second / ˈsekənd / adj, adv. next after first
• February is the second month of the year.
72. simple / ˈsɪmp əl / adj. easy to do or understand
• Its simple to find our house.
• I want an explanation, but make it simple.
73. singular / ˈsɪŋɡjələr / adj. the form of a word that you use for one person or thing
• The singular of men is man.
74. span / spæn / n. the length of time that something continues
• Average life span in Japan is of 85 years.
75. stay / steɪ / v. to continue in the same way and not change
• Can you stay after work to play tennis?
76. take care of / teɪk keər ɒv / v. to deal with something
• The roads are icy, take care of yourselves.
77. teach / tiːtʃ / v. to give lessons to students, for example in a school or college
• She teaches English to foreign students.
78. together / təˈɡeðər / adv. with each other or close to each other
• Sharzad and Hesam usually walk home together.
79. travel / ˈtrævəl / v. to go from one place to another
• He travelled over 1,000 miles to be at the wedding.
80. trip / trɪp / n. a journey to a place and back again
• Were going on a trip to Norway this summer.
81. underline / ˌʌndərˈlaɪn / v. to draw a line under a word or words; to emphasize
• Underline all the technical words in red, please.
82. visit / ˈvɪzɪt / v. to go to see a person or place for a short time
• She visited me in hospital.
83. visitor / ˈvɪzɪtər / n. a person who goes to see another person or a place for a short time
• You have some visitors to see you.
84. voluntary / ˈvɑːlənteri / adj. without being forced or paid to do something
• He does voluntary work at a childrens hospital.
85. wild / waɪəld / adj. plants and animals live or grow in nature, not with people, violent
• We picked some wild flowers.

sections.title: English to English Dictionary (Lesson Two)
lines: 1. above / əˈbʌv / adv, prep. in or to a higher place; higher than somebody or something
• Theres a mirror above the sink.
2. actually / ˈæktʃuəli / adv. in fact or really
• I didnt actually see her - I just heard her voice.
3. against / əˈɡeɪnst / prep. disagreeing with a plan or activity
• She spoke against my decision.
4. amazing / əˈmeɪzɪŋ / adj. extremely surprising
• Rain forests are filled with amazing creatures.
5. ant / ænt / n. a very small insect that lives in big groups in the ground and works very hard
• He studied the behavior of ants.
6. appropriate / əˈproʊpriət / adj. suitable for a particular situation or occasion; proper
• Is this film appropriate for small children?
• Jeans and T-shirts are not appropriate for a job interview.
7. area / ˈeriə / n. a part of a town, country or the world; zone
• Do you live in this area?
8. immigrant / ˈɪməɡrənt / n. a person who comes to another country to live there
• Many immigrants to Britain have come from Asia.
9. attack / əˈtæk / v. to try to hurt or defeat using violence
• Most wild animals wont attack unless they are provoked.
10. bacteria / bækˈtɪriə / n. very small things that live in air, water, earth, plants and animals.
• There are many different types of bacteria.
11. because / bɪˈkɑːz / conj. for the reason that
• He was angry because I was late.
12. blank / blæŋk / n. with no writing, pictures or anything else on it
• Sign your name in the blank space at the bottom of the form.
13. blood / blʌd / n. the red liquid inside your body
• She lost a lot of blood in the accident.
• The police found traces of blood on his jacket.
14. body / ˈbɑːdi / n. the physical structure of a person or animal
• My fingers were numb and my whole body ached.
15. bore / bɔːr / v. to make somebody feel bored, especially by talking too much
• He bores everyone with his long stories.
16. boring / ˈbɔːrɪŋ / adj. not interesting
• Its boring to sit on the plane with nothing to read.
17. both / bəʊθ / pron. the two; not only one but also the other
• Both my parents are teachers.
18. brain / breɪn / n. the part inside the head of a person or an animal that thinks and feels
• Marie has an amazing brain.
19. brave / breɪv / adj. ready to do dangerous or difficult things without fear
• She was very brave to learn to ski at 50.
20. carry / ˈkæri / v. to hold something and take it to another place or keep it with you
• He carried the suitcase to my room.
21. cell / sel / n. the smallest basic unit of a plant or animal
• The doctors discovered cancerous cells.
22. cheap / tʃiːp / adj. costing little money
• That restaurant is very good and quite cheap.
23. clear / klɪər / adj. easy to understand, hear, read, or see
• She spoke in a loud, clear voice.
• Our new television has a very clear picture.
24. collect / kəˈlekt / v. to take things from different people or places and put them together
• The waiter collected the dirty glasses.
• When did you start collecting antique glass?
25. compare / kəmˈper / v. to examine the difference between two or more things
• Compare your answers with Ahmads.
26. cross / krɑːs / v. to go across from one side of something to the other
• Its not a good place to cross the road.
27. dangerous / ˈdeɪndʒərəs / adj. A person or thing that is dangerous may hurt you.
• The men are armed and dangerous.
28. deep / diːp / adj. being of a particular distance from the top to the bottom
• Be careful: the water is very deep.
29. defend / dɪˈfɛnd / v. to fight to keep away people or things that attack
• They defended the city against the enemy.
30. describe / diˈskraɪb / v. to say what somebody or something is like or what happened
• Can you describe the man you saw?
31. difficult / ˈdɪfəkəlt / adj. not easy to do or understand
• The noise outside made it difficult to concentrate.
32. disease / dɪˈziːz / n. (an) illness of people, animals, etc., caused by infection or a failure
• There is no known cure for this disease.
• Malaria and measles are diseases.
33. donate / dəʊˈneɪt / v. to give something, especially money, to people who need it
• The appeal for people to donate blood was very successful.
34. drop / drɑːp / v. to fall or to allow something to fall
• The book dropped from/off the shelf.
n. a very small amount of liquid
• There were little drops of paint on the kitchen floor.
35. easy / ˈiː.zi / adj. not difficult to do or understand
• The homework was very easy.
• She doesnt find it easy to talk about her problems.
36. element / ˈeləmənt / n. an important part of something
• Cost was an important element in our decision.
37. exercise / ˈeksərsaɪz / n. a short piece of written work to practice sth you are learning
• The book has exercises at the end of every chapter.
v. moving your body to keep it strong and well
• Swimming is a very good exercise.
38. expensive / ɪkˈspensɪv / adj. costly, high-priced, high-cost
• Photography is an expensive hobby.
39. fact / fækt / n. something that you know has happened or is true
• I dont know all the facts about the case.
40. famous / ˈfeɪm əs / adj. known by many people
• Oxford is famous for its university
41. fight / faɪt / v. When people fight, they try to hurt or kill each other.
• Our grandfather fought in the war.
42. fill / fɪl / v. to make something full
• Can you fill this glass with water, please?
43. gift / ɡɪft / n. a present or something that is given
• The earrings were a gift from my aunt.
44. great / greɪt / adj. very good; very large; excellent
• The movie was a great success.
• A: How are you feeling now? B: Great.
45. grow / ɡrəʊ / v. a. to become bigger
• Children grow very quickly.
• This plant grows best in the shade.
v. to become; get
• It is growing dark.
46. half / hɑːf / n, adj. one of two equal parts of something; ½
• She was born in the latter half of the 18th century.
• Half of six is three.
47. happen / ˈhæp ən / v. to take place, usually without being planned first; occur
• How did the accident happen?
• A funny thing happened in the office today.
48. head / hed / n. the part of your body above your neck
• Put this hat on to keep your head warm.
49. healthy / ˈhelθi / adj. well; not often ill
• Shes a normal, healthy child.
50. heavy / ˈhevi / adj. weighing a lot; difficult to lift or move
• I cant carry this bag – its too heavy.
51. important / ɪmˈpɔːrtənt / adj. necessary or of great value;
• It is important to sleep well the night before an exam.
52. in fact / ɪn fækt / really; acutally
• In fact, shes now taking an advanced driving test.
53. information / ˌɪnfəˈmeɪʃən / n. facts about people or things
• Do you have any information about/on train times?
54. interested / ˈɪntrəstɪd / adj. wanting to know more about somebody or something
• Are you interested in animals?
55. irregular / ɪˈreɡjələr / adj. not according to usual rules or what is expected
• Catch is an irregular verb.
56. keep / kiːp / v. to stay in a particular state or condition; to put or store sth in a particular place
• Where do you keep the coffee?
57. late / leɪt / adj, adv. near the end of a time
• They arrived in the late afternoon.
• It was late at night.
58. laugh / læf / v. to make sounds with your voice
• Maria looked at him and laughed.
• His jokes always make me laugh.
59. liquid / ˈlɪkwɪd / n. a substance that is not a solid or a gas, for example water or milk
• Add a little more liquid to the sauce.
60. move / muːv / v. to change from one place or position to another.
• Could you move your car, please? Its blocking the road.
• Dont get off the bus while its moving.
61. nation / ˈneɪʃən / n. a country and all the people who live in it
• We are an independent nation.
62. neat / niːt / adj. tidy and carefully arranged; clean
• His clothes were always neat and clean.
63. need / niːd / v, n. to have to have something or someone; require
• Theres an urgent need for more nurses.
64. neighbor / ˈneɪbər / n. someone who lives next to you or near you
• Our next-door neighbours say theyll look after our cat for us while were away.
65. nothing / ˈnʌθɪŋ / pron. not anything
• Theres nothing in this bottle – its empty.
66. observatory / əbˈzɜːrvətəri / n. a building from which scientists can watch the planets, etc.
• We work in the same observatory.
67. only / ˈəʊnli / adj. with no others
• Shes the only girl in her class.
• Is this really the only way to do it?
68. orbit / ˈɔːrbɪt / v. to move around something in space; turn around
• The spacecraft is orbiting the moon.
69. organ / ˈɔːrɡən / n. a part of your body that has a special purpose, for example heart
• Your ears, eyes, tongue, nose and skin are your sense organs.
70. own / əʊn / pronoun, v. belonging to or done by a particular person
• She makes all her own clothes.
71. paint / peɪnt / n, v. to cover a surface with paint
• Weve painted the bedroom blue.
72. polite / pəˈlaɪt / adj. speaking or behaving in a way that shows respect
• It is polite to say please when you ask for something.
• Shes always very polite.
73. powerful / ˈpaʊəfəl / adj. having a lot of strength or power; strong
• The car has a very powerful engine.
• The president is more powerful than the prime minister.
74. problem / ˈprɒbləm / n. something that is difficult; something that makes you worry
• She has a lot of problems. Her husband is ill and her son is in prison.
75. pump / pʌm / v. to force a gas or a liquid to go in a particular direction
• Your heart pumps blood around your body.
76. quality / ˈkwɒləti / n. how good or bad something is
• The quality of her work is excellent.
77. really / ˈrɪəli / adv. in fact; actually
• Do you really love him?
78. ring / rɪŋ / a. a circle of metal that you wear on your finger a wedding ring
v. the act of making a phone call to someone
• I ring home once a week to tell my parents Im okay.
79. rocky / ˈrɑː.ki / adj. with a lot of rocks
• She scrambled along the rocky path.
80. sleep / sliːp / v. to rest with your eyes closed, as you do at night
• I sleep for eight hours every night
81. strange / streɪndʒ / adj. unusual or surprising
• Did you hear that strange noise?
82. type / taɪp / n. a group of things that are the same in some way
• What type of clothes does she wear?
83. under / ˈʌndər / prep. in or to a place that is lower than or below something
• The cat is under the table.
84. useful / ˈjuːsfəl / adj. good and helpful for doing something
• This bag will be useful for carrying my books.
85. vessel / ˈvesəl / n. any of the tubes through which blood flows in the body
• One of the blood vessels in his heart needs urgent operation.
86. village / ˈvɪlɪdʒ / n. a group of houses that is smaller than a town, usually in the countryside
• She lives in a village in the mountains.
87. virus / ˈvaɪərəs / n. a living thing that is small to see but that can make you ill
• a flu virus
88. without / wɪðˈaʊt / prep. not having, showing or using something
• Its cold – dont go out without your coat.
89. wonderful / ˈwʌnd ə fəl / adj. very good
• What a wonderful present!
90. wooden / ˈwʊdən / adj. made of wood
• She keeps the toys in a wooden box.
91. world / wɜːld / n. the earth and all the people, places, and things on it
• Different parts of the world have very different climatic conditions.
92. worry / ˈwʌri / v. to feel that sth bad will happen or has happened; make sb feel this
• Theres nothing to worry about.
Note

sections.title: English to English Dictionary (Lesson Three)
lines: 1. again / əˈɡen / adv. one more time; once more
• Could you spell your name again, please?
2. age / eɪdʒ / n. the amount of time that somebody or something has been in the world
• Shes getting very forgetful in her old age.
3. airplane / ˈerpleɪn / n. a vehicle designed for air travel that has wings with engine
• She has her own private airplane.
4. alone / əˈləʊn / adj, adv. without other people
• She decided to climb the mountain alone.
5. amazing / əˈmeɪzɪŋ / adj. extremely surprising
• Its amazing that no one else has applied for the job.
6. another / əˈnʌðər / adj. a different thing or person
• Would you like another drink?
• I cant see you tomorrow – can we meet another day?
7. antibiotic / ˌænti̬ baɪˈɑːtɪ̬ k / n. a medicine which fights illness in a persons body
• The doctor gave me some antibiotics for a chest infection.
8. appropriate / əˈprəʊpriət / adj. suitable or right for a particular situation, person, etc
• Jeans and T-shirts are not appropriate for a job interview.
9. ashamed / əˈʃeɪmd / adj. feeling sorry and unhappy because you have done sth wrong
• I felt so ashamed of myself for making such a fuss.
10. answer / ˈænsər / n. a reaction to a question, letter, phone call, etc.
• We need a definite answer by tomorrow.
v. to say, write, or do something as a reaction to a question, letter, etc. ; reply
• I couldnt answer all the exam questions.
11. attend / əˈtend / v. to go officially and usually regularly to a place
• She is going to attend the conference.
12. behave / biˈheɪv / v. to do and say things in a certain way
• They behaved very kindly towards me.
13. belief / bɪˈliːf / n. something that you believe
• His belief in God gave him hope during difficult times.
14. believe / bɪˈliːv / v. to think that something is true, correct, or real
• He believes that all children are born with equal intelligence.
15. camera / ˈkæmrə / n. a device for taking photographs or making films or TV programmes
• Hes just bought a new digital camera.
16. change / tʃeɪndʒ / n. the act of becoming different
• Theyve made a lot of changes to the house.
v. to become different
• Water changes into ice when it is very cold.
17. dear / dɪər / adj. loved or liked very much
• Iran is a very dear country for all of us.
18. develop / diˈveləp / v. to grow slowly, increase, or change into something else
• This exercise is designed to develop the shoulder and back muscles.
19. during / ˈdʒʊərɪŋ / prep. all the time that something is happening
• They work during the night and sleep by day.
20. end / end / n. the last part of something
• Turn right at the end of the street.
v. to finish or stop, or to make something finish or stop
• She ended her speech at 10 p.m.
21. energetic / ˌenəˈdʒetɪk / adj. full of energy so that you can do a lot of things
• Hes very energetic for a man of his age.
22. experiment / ɪkˈsperəmənt / n. a test done to learn sth or to discover if sth works or is true
• They have to do experiments to find out if the drug is safe for humans.
23. express / ɪkˈspres / v. to show a feeling, opinion, or fact
• She expressed her ideas well.
24. feel / fiːl / v. to know something because your body tells you
• I never feel safe when Richard is driving.
25. find / faɪnd / v. to see or get something after looking or trying
• I cant find my glasses.
• I couldnt find Andrews phone number.
26. flu / fluː / n. an illness like a very bad cold that makes your body sore and hot
• I think Ive got flu.
27. fortunately / ˈfɔːrtʃənətli / adv. luckily
• I fortunately got the job.
28. fun / fʌn / n. Have fun (= enjoy yourself)!
• Im just learning English for fun.
adj. enjoyable
• There are lots of fun things to do here.
29. give up / ɡɪv ʌp / v. to stop trying to guess
• After ten minutes trying to get the answer I gave up.
• I give up - tell me the answer!
30. get around / ɡet əˈraʊnd / v. to travel to a lot of places
• I will get around Spain this week.
31. grow up / ɡroʊ ʌp / v. to gradually become an adult
• She grew up in England.
32. heavily / ˈhevəli / adv. to a great degree
• The country depends heavily on foreign aid.
33. herself / hɜːˈself / pron. a word that makes she stronger
• She herself admitted that it was wrong.
34. hospital / ˈhɑː.spɪtə̬ l / n. a place where doctors and nurses look after people who are ill or hurt
• My brother is in hospital – hes broken his leg.
35. human / ˈhjuːmən / adj . connected with people, not animals or machines
• Governments should respect human rights.
36. idea / aɪˈdɪə / n. a suggestion or plan for doing something; opinion
• Its not a good idea to drive for hours without a rest.
37. interview / ˈɪntəvjuː / a meeting in which sb asks you questions to see if you are suitable for a job
or course
• He is very good at interviewing people.
38. invent / ɪnˈvent / v. to make or think of something for the first time, to create a reason, excuse
story, etc. that is not true
• But I didnt invent the story - everything I told you is true.
39. jump / dʒʌmp / v.to push yourself suddenly off the ground and into the air using your legs
• The children were jumping up and down with excitement.
40. key / kiː / n. a piece of metal that opens or closes a lock
• He turned the key and opened the door.
adj. very important and having a lot of influence on other people or things
• I think there is one key fact that you have come here.
41. kid / kɪd / n. a child
• He took the kids to the park while I was working.
42. knowledge / ˈnɑːlɪdʒ / n. understanding of or information about a subject that you get by
experience or study
• He has a good knowledge of European history.
• I only have a limited knowledge of Spanish.
43. laboratory / ˈlæbrətɔːri / n. a special room where scientists work
• Laboratory tests suggest that the new drug may be used to treat cancer.
44. light / laɪt / n, adj. a piece of equipment that produces light; not heavy
• Turn the light on.
• Take this bag - its quite light.
45. medicine / ˈmedsən / n. the science of understanding illnesses and making sick people well again
• Hes studying medicine.
• She is a doctor, but is unable to practice medicine.
46. narrate / ˈnæreɪt / v. to tell a story, often by reading aloud from a text, or to describe events as
they happen
• One by one the witnesses narrated the sequence of events.
47. near / nɪər / adj. not far away; close to somebody or something
• Lets walk to my house. Its quite near.
48. noise / nɔɪz / n. a sound, especially one that is loud or unpleasant
• I heard a loud noise and ran to the window.
49. observe / əbˈzɜːrv / v. to watch or see somebody or something
• The police observed a man leaving the house.
50. pain / peɪn / n. a feeling of physical suffering caused by injury or illness; unhappiness
• Her eyes were full of pain.
• I felt a sharp pain in my foot.
51. pass away / pæs ə ˈweɪ / v. to die
• Shes terribly upset because her father passed away last week.
52. patient / ˈpeɪʃ(ə)nt / n. a sick person that a doctor is looking after
• The patient didnt arrive to the clinic on time.
53. personality / ˌpɜːsənˈæləti / n. the type of person you are, shown by the way you behave, feel
and think
• She has a very warm personality.
54. possible / ˈpɑːsəbəl / adj. able to happen or to be done
• Is it possible to buy tickets in advance?
55. power / paʊər / n. ability to control people and events, strength
• Ive no power over him - he does what he wants to.
• Id like to help but I dont have the power.
56. publish / ˈpʌblɪʃ / v. to prepare and print a book, magazine or newspaper for selling
• This dictionary was published by Oxford University Press.
• She was only 19 when her first novel was published.
57. quit / kwɪt / v. to leave a job or place; to stop doing something
• Hes going to quit smoking.
58. recite / rɪˈsaɪt / v. to say a piece of writing aloud from memory
• She recited the peom very easily.
59. research / rɪˈsɜːrtʃ / v. to study a subject in detail, especially in order to discover new information
or reach a new understanding
• Shes researching into possible cures for AIDS.
• Scientists are researching the causes of the disease.
60. researcher / rɪˈsɜː.tʃər / n. a person studying a subject in detail, especially in order to discover new
information
• Researchers are constantly studying deep space.
61. sadly / ˈsædli / adv. in an unhappy way
• She looked sadly at the empty house.
62. scientist / saɪentɪst / n. an expert who studies or works in one of the sciences
• Scientists say that the results of the research are not perfect.
63. situation / ˌsɪtʃuˈeɪʃən / n. the things that are happening in a certain place or at a certain time
• Her news put me in a difficult situation.
• We are in a difficult situation.
64. solve / sɑːlv / v. to find the answer to a question or problem
• She finally solved the math problem.
65. success / səkˈses / n. something that achieves positive results
• The film The Matrix was a great success.
66. translate / trænsˈleɪt / v. to change words into a different language
• Can you translate this letter into English for me?
• I couldnt translate the poem into English.
67. translator / trænsˈleɪtər / adj. a person who translates
• I work as a translator in this office.
68. try / traɪ / v. to make an effort to do something
• I tried to remember her name but I couldnt.
• We must try to spend less money.
69. wait / weɪt / v. to stay in one place until sth happens or until sb or sth comes
• There were a lot of people waiting to use the phone.
70. weak / wiːk / adj. not physically powerful or strong
• She felt very weak after her long illness.
71. while / waɪl / conj. during the time that
• The telephone rang while I was having a shower.
Note

sections.title: English to English Dictionary (Lesson Four)
lines: 1. abroad / əˈbrɔːd , əˈbrɑːd / adv. in or to another country
• Are you going abroad this summer?
• She lives abroad.
2. across / əˈkrɑːs / adv, prep. from one side to the other side of something
• The river was about twenty meters across.
• Theyre building a new bridge across the river.
3. actually / ˈæktʃuəli / adv. really; in fact
• I didnt actually see her - I just heard her voice.
• Its unclear what actually happened that night.
4. ancient / ˈeɪnʃənt / adj. very old; from a time long ago
• That photo makes me look ancient!
• She is a professor of ancient history.
5. angry / ˈæŋɡri / adj. having a strong feeling against someone who has behaved badly
• Please dont be angry with me
• Jesse laughed, which made me even angrier.
6. arrive / əˈraɪv / v. to come to a place
• They arrived at the station ten minutes late.
• What time did you arrive home?
7. attract / əˈtrækt / v. to make somebody like somebody or something
• He was attracted to her.
• The circus is attracting huge crowds.
8. attraction / əˈtrækʃən / n. a feeling of liking somebody or something very much
• I cant understand his attraction to her.
• Buckingham Palace is a major tourist attraction.
9. attractive / əˈtræktɪv / adj. very pleasing in appearance or sound
• Hes very attractive.
• Thats an attractive offer.
10. baggage / ˈbæɡɪdʒ / n. bags and suitcases that you take with you when you travel
• Can we leave our baggage at the hotel until it is time to leave for the airport?
11. behavior / bɪˈheɪvjər / n. the way you are; the way that you do and say things
• He was sent out of the class for his bad behaviour.
12. bravely / breɪvli / adv. ready to do dangerous or difficult things without fear
• He fought bravely in the war.
• The policeman entered the building bravely and arrested the thief.
13. burn / bɝːn / v. to make flames and heat; to be on fire
• She escaped from the burning building.
• He was badly burned in the blaze.
14. ceremony / ˈserəməni / n. a formal public or religious event
• We werent married in church, but we had a civil ceremony in a registry office.
15. cheap / tʃiːp / adj. costing little money
• That restaurant is very good and quite cheap.
• Computers are getting cheaper all the time.
16. check / tʃek / v. to look at something to see that it is right, good or safe
• Before driving off, I checked the oil and water.
• Check that all the windows are closed before you leave.
17. cruel / ˈkruːəl / adj. extremely unkind and unpleasant and causing pain to people or animals
• Children can be very cruel to each other.
• I think its cruel to keep animals in cages.
18. culture / ˈkʌltʃər / n. the customs, ideas and way of life of of people or a country
• American culture has been exported all over the world.
19. desert / ˈdezərt / n. a large, dry area of land with very few plants
• They were lost in the desert for nine days.
• The Sahara Desert is in Africa.
20. destination / ˌdestəˈneɪʃən / n. the place where somebody or something is going
• They were very tired when they finally reached their destination.
• The Caribbean is a popular holiday destination.
21. domestic / dəˈmestɪk / adj. not international; inside a country; connected with home
• Domestic opinion had turned against the war.
• Many cats and dogs are domestic animals.
22. embassy / ˈembəsi / n. the people who represent their country in a foreign country
• To get a visa, you should apply to the American embassy.
• Rebel soldiers overran the embassy last night.
23. emphasis / ˈemfəsɪs / n. special importance that is given to something
• Our school places a lot of emphasis on science.
• The emphasis is on the final syllable.
24. enjoy / ɪnˈdʒɔɪ / v. to like something very much
• I enjoy playing football
• Did you enjoy your dinner?
25. check in / tʃekɪn / v. to tell the person at the desk in a hotel or an airport that you have arrived
• I have to check in an hour before my flight.
26. chip / tʃɪp / n. a long piece of potato cooked in hot oil
• We had fish and chips for lunch.
27. choice / tʃɔɪs / n. the act of choosing between two or more people or things
• You made the right choice.
• We have no choice. We have to leave.
28. comfortable / ˈkʌmfɚtə̬ bəl / adj. nice to sit in, to be in, or to wear
• This is a very comfortable bed
• These office chairs arent at all comfortable.
29. compare / kəmˈper / v. to examine or look for the difference between two or more things
. Children learn more interesting things compared to when we were at school.
30. continent / ˈkɑːntə̬ nənt / n. one of the seven main areas of land in the world
• The continents make up about 35% of the earths crust.
• He decided to cycle across the continent to raise money for charity.
31. contrast / kɑːntræst / n. a difference between things that you can see
• There is an obvious contrast between the cultures of East and West.
32. cookie / ˈkʊki / n. a small, flat, sweet food made from flour and sugar
• This recipe makes three dozen cookies.
33. course / kɔːrs / n. a set of classes or a plan of study on a certain subject
• I did a course in creative writing.
• I finished the course last month.
34. entertainment / entə̬ ˈteɪnmənt / n. films / movies, music, etc. used to entertain people; hobby
• There will be live entertainment at the party.
• The entertainment was provided by a folk band.
35. expensive / ɪkˈspensɪv / adj. costing a lot of money
• The meal was very expensive .
• Art books are expensive to produce.
36. experience / ɪkˈspɪriəns / n. knowing about something because you have seen it or done it
• She has four years teaching experience.
37. familiar with / fəˈmɪlijɚ wɪð / adj. that you know well
• Im not familiar with this computer.
38. flight / flaɪt / n. a journey in a plane
• Our flight leaves at 10 a.m.
• a direct flight from London to Singapore.
39. flu / fluː / n. an illness like a very bad cold that makes your body sore and hot
• The whole family has the flu.
40. foreign / ˈfɔːrən / adj. belonging to or connected with a country that is not your own
• You could tell she was foreign by the way she dressed.
• Weve got some foreign students staying at our house.
41. generous / ˈdʒenərəs / adj. always ready to give people things or to spend money
• It was generous of him to offer to pay for us both.
• It was generous of your parents to pay for the meal.
42. health / helθ / n. the condition of your body
• Smoking can seriously damage your health.
43. historical / hɪˈstɔːrɪkəl / adj. connected with real people or events in the past
• She writes historical novels.
44. honestly / ˈɑːnɪstli / adv. in a way that is honest
• I honestly cant remember a thing about last night.
45. hospitable / hɑːˈspɪtə̬ bəl / adj. friendly and kind to visitors
• The local people are very hospitable to strangers.
• He thanked Patricia for being such a hospitable hostess.
46. host / hoʊst / n. a person who invites people to their house, for example to a party
• She thanked the hosts for their hospitality
47. image / ˈɪmɪdʒ / n. the impression that a person or an organization gives to the public
• His public image is very different from the real person.
48. international / ˌɪntərˈnæʃənəl / adj. between different countries
• Words like bank, hotel, police, ... are international.
49. irregular / ɪˈreɡjələr / adj. happening at different times
• He visited his parents at irregular intervals.
50. junk food / ˈdʒʌŋk ˌfuːd / adj. food that is quick and easy to prepare and eat but that is bad for your
health
• Some parents warn their kids not to eat junk foods at all.
51. leave / liːv / v. to go away from a place or a person
• The plane leaves Boston at 12.35.
52. local / ˈloʊ.kəl / adj. of a place near you
• Her children go to the local school.
53. locate / loʊˈkeɪt / v. find the place of ...
• The mechanic located the fault immediately.
54. meal / miːl / n. food that you eat at a certain time of the day
• We had a nice meal in that restaurant.
55. mean / miːn / v. to express something such as an idea or fact
• The red light means that you have to stop here.
56. meet / miːt / v. to come together by chance or because you have planned it
• I met Kate in the library today.
• Lets meet outside the cinema at eight oclock.
57. midnight / ˈmɪdnaɪt / n. twelve oclock at night
• We left the party at midnight.
• She heard the clock strike midnight.
58. online / ˈɑːnlaɪn / adj. using a computer or the Internet
• Online shopping is both cheap and convenient.
• Bookings can be made online.
59. paradise / ˈperədaɪs / n. place where some people think good people go after they die
• This mall is a shoppers paradise.
60. polite / pəˈlaɪt / adj. speaking or behaving in a way that shows respect
• It is polite to say please when you ask for something.
61. popular / pɒpjələr / adj. liked by a lot of people
• Football is a popular sport in Britain.
62. prefer / prɪˈfɜːr / v. to like one thing or person better than another
• He prefers going out to studying.
63. prepare / prɪˈper / v. to make somebody or something ready; to make yourself ready
• Martin is in the kitchen preparing the dinner.
64. probable / ˈprɑːbəbəl / adj. likely to happen or to be true
• It is probable that the disease has a genetic element.
65. probably / ˈprɑːbəbəli / adv. almost certainly
• I will probably see you on Thursday.
66. pyramid / ˈpɪrəmɪd / n. a shape with a flat bottom and 3 sides that come to a point at the top
• the pyramids of Egypt
67. respect / rɪˈspekt / n. thinking that somebody or something is very good or clever
• I have the greatest respect for your brother.
68. rudely / ruːdli / v. not polite
• You must not treat rudely to others.
69. site / saɪt / n. a place where a building is, was, or will be
• This house was built on the site of an old theatre.
70. souvenir / ˌsuːvəˈnɪr / adj. sth that you keep to remember a place or a special event
• I brought back this cowboy hat as a souvenir of Texas.
• I bought the ring as a souvenir of Greece.
71. suggestion / səˈdʒestʃən / n. an idea, plan, or action that is suggested
• They didnt like my suggestion that we should all share the cost.
72. suitable / ˈsuːtəbəl / adj. right for somebody or something
• This film isnt suitable for children.
73. surf / sɜːrf / v. to use the internet
• He spends a lot of time surfing the internet/ Net/Web.
• Janes been surfing the Web all morning.
74. tower / taʊər / n a tall narrow building or a tall part of a building
• From the top of the tower, the outlook over the city was breathtaking.
75. travel / ˈtrævəl / v. to go from one place to another
• I travel to school by bus.
• I go to bed early if Im traveling the next day.
76. understand / ˌʌndərˈstænd / v. to know what sth means or why sth happens; find out
• I dont understand why youre so angry.
77. vacation / veɪˈkeɪʃən / n. a period of time when you are not working or studying
• You look tired—you should take a vacation.
• The job includes two weeks paid vacation.
78. wonderful / ˈwʌndɚfəl / adj. very good
• We had a wonderful time last night.
• Its wonderful what you can do when you have to.
Irregular Verbs افعال بی‌قاعده
